What is checked, and why

Buyer identification. Under the UAE e-invoicing system every B2B e-invoice carries the buyer's Tax Registration Number and address; the Peppol identifier is built from the TIN. A missing or malformed TRN is the single most common reason an invoice will fail validation at the buyer's provider. UAE TRNs are 15 digits and begin with 100.
Tax categories. Each line needs a VAT category: standard 5%, zero-rated, exempt, out of scope, reverse charge or designated zone. A zero-VAT line with no category cannot be classified and is rejected; a 5% line whose VAT does not equal 5% of the taxable amount fails arithmetic validation.
Credit notes and numbering. Reductions, cancellations and refunds must be issued as electronic credit notes referencing the original invoice; negative invoices are not a document type. Invoice numbers must be unique.
Currency and precision. Foreign-currency invoices must carry the VAT amount in AED; amounts beyond two decimals fail schema checks.
What this is not. A screening of your exported data against the published mandatory fields and arithmetic rules, in your browser, with nothing sent anywhere. It is not a provider's validator and not legal or tax advice; your provider's sandbox is the final test.
Rules from Ministerial Decision 243 of 2025, the MoF Electronic Invoicing Guidelines v1.1 and the Electronic Invoice Mandatory Field Requirements v1.0. Independent and free; no provider is promoted. Companion to the UAE ASP Selector.
